Daily Brief

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz faces mounting political pressure after his CDU party suffered historic defeats in two state elections Sunday, failing to enter parliament in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern for the first time in 77 years while the far-right AfD surged [BBC, Le Monde, France 24]. Russia's parliamentary elections delivered an expected victory for United Russia, expanding its constitutional majority despite over four years of war in Ukraine, with the only anti-war party Yabloko barred from the ballot [BBC, The Hindu]. Ukraine launched its largest drone attack on Moscow, with 450 drones targeting the capital's oil refinery and causing civilian casualties, as President Trump reportedly pressures Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure [BBC, France 24, Financial Times]. In Ethiopia, seven armed groups including the TPLF and Fano militias formed an unprecedented alliance seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government, raising fears of renewed civil war [BBC, RFI]. Three major US news outlets—CNN, Politico, and MS NOW—announced they will sue the Trump administration over their White House ban, citing First Amendment violations [BBC, Financial Times]. World leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly, with key bilateral meetings expected between Trump and leaders including Macron, Burnham, and Zelensky amid ongoing conflicts in Iran and Ukraine [Globe and Mail, RFI].
